method: Wash the vegetables. Chop onion and peppers where listed; slice tomato where listed and keep raw meat preparation separate.
Cut the 120g baby potatoes into roughly 1 cm cubes. Simmer in a saucepan of water for about 6–8 minutes, continuing until a knife enters the centre easily. Drain thoroughly and let steam escape.

Use half the measured olive oil in a frying pan. Dice the chicken into roughly 2 cm pieces. Cook the chicken breast thoroughly, turning regularly. Check the thickest piece is steaming hot through the centre. A clean probe should read 70°C for 2 minutes. The chicken must have no pink flesh and its juices should run clear. Transfer to a clean plate.

Heat the remaining half of the measured olive oil in the frying pan. Add the drained potatoes and turn occasionally until golden. Add the tomato, spinach, onion; cook until softened, with spinach wilted and excess liquid evaporated where listed.
Return the fully cooked chicken breast to the pan and heat through.

Heat the sandwich toaster. Spoon the cooked filling between the measured bread slices, spreading it evenly and keeping wetter ingredients away from the edges. Do not overfill; serve any remaining cooked filling alongside.
Toast for around 4–6 minutes, following the appliance guidance, until the bread is crisp and the filling is steaming hot in the centre. Rest for one minute before cutting.
Serve the toastie with any remaining measured filling. Nutrition includes the whole portion, including the side.
